# Access patterns

How a person reaches a legacy system, by what the system can accept.

## P-A: Protocol bastion

- When: The system is reached through SSH, RDP, VNC, a database console, Kubernetes or a web UI.
- Path: person -> bastion -> legacy (flows F-03, F-04, F-06, F-07, F-10)
- Governance: KeyClerk grants a lease and signs it into the edge's bundle; the agent turns it into a Warpgate role assignment that expires with the lease (C-01) and approves sessions the lease covers (C-02).
- Evidence: Warpgate session recording (streamed off the edge, F-09); KeyClerk signed change log.

## P-E: Engineering workstation

- When: The system can only be worked with a vendor engineering suite or an OT protocol the bastion cannot carry (Modbus/TCP, S7comm, EtherNet/IP, OPC-DA, TIA Portal, Studio 5000); decision 0019.
- Path: person -> bastion -> legacy (flows F-03, F-04, F-06, F-07, F-10)
- Governance: The plant-owned workstation inside the system's zone is a target like any other (privileged by default): a lease, RDP through Warpgate, KeyClerk's session-start approval by someone on site, the session on the edge's local page. The workstation's own conduit to the controllers is declared and signed by the system owner; a safety system is a separate entitlement. ReliKey carries no network reach into the zone. Variant (0020): a diagnostic workstation whose conduit the plant makes read-only (an industrial firewall allowing only read functions per device, unit and address, or a one-way replica), declared and owner-signed; ReliKey records the declaration and claims nothing about the controller's state. ReliKey writes no industrial protocol parser.
- Evidence: Warpgate's recording of the workstation session (F-09); KeyClerk signed change log and approval proof.
- Residual: Inside the session the workstation's tools can do whatever they can to the controllers it reaches; the recording shows it, the lease and approval bound who and when. The workstation's patching and hardening are the plant's.

## P-F: Legacy client jump target

- When: The system is reached only by a client the bastion cannot carry: telnet or rlogin, a Java applet or KVM console, or serial where no console server fits; decision 0024. Serial goes to a console server with SSH per port first (P-A); old TLS to a firmware update, then a re-terminator in the zone behind an HTTPS target (P-A).
- Path: person -> bastion -> legacy (flows F-03, F-04, F-06, F-07, F-10)
- Governance: A hardened plant host inside one zone (never dual-homed), holding only the old clients, is a target like any other (privileged by default): a lease, SSH through Warpgate for telnet, rlogin and serial (text recording), RDP for Java and KVM consoles (video), session-start approval as for P-E. Its conduit and the zone-internal plaintext leg to each device are declared and signed by the system owner. No port, agent or X11 forwarding, no sftp or scp, no RDP clipboard, drive or USB redirection; kiosk browser on an allowlist; rebuilt from a signed image. ReliKey writes no protocol code for it.
- Evidence: Warpgate's recording of the jump target session (F-09; whether SSH input is kept is a lab fact to establish); KeyClerk signed change log and approval proof.
- Residual: The old clients are weak by nature; containment and rebuilds bound a compromise. Concurrent people share the target's one account until the account mapping is established (one session at a time meanwhile). The old system's shared credential is rotated by its owner after each lease or is a named residual. Java and KVM consoles are evidenced as video only.

## P-B: LDAP lease credential

- When: The system has its own login that can only check a password with an LDAP bind.
- Path: person -> proxy -> bastion -> legacy (flows F-02, F-03b, F-03c, F-06, F-08, F-10, F-11)
- Governance: The person reaches the system's login through a Warpgate target (web UI as HTTPS, a thick client on a jump host behind RDP) and types the lease credential (decision 0008). The system binds against the edge's facade instead of the old directory. For a lease, the agent sets the person's facade password to a fresh random value (C-03), shown once on the desk after a fresh passkey sign-in, and rotates it again at lease end; outside a lease no known password exists. The account name stays the same, so the system's own user mapping is unchanged.
- Evidence: KeyClerk change log (lease, hand-over, rotation); facade bind log reported by the agent.
- Residual: Between hand-over and lease end the credential is a password the person can copy. Short leases, rotation at session end or lease end, one holder per account (R-15); per-user injection only once Warpgate offers it (U-09).

## P-C: Web front with injected identity

- When: A web application that trusts an authenticating proxy (header or basic auth).
- Path: person -> proxy -> bastion -> legacy (flows F-03b, F-03c, F-04, F-06, F-07, F-10)
- Governance: As P-A; the bastion's HTTPS target carries the identity. Header trust is decision register R-05.
- Evidence: Warpgate HTTPS session log.

## P-D: Machine panel (HMI) with an LDAP login

- When: A machine, robot or appliance whose own touch panel or local console signs people in with an LDAP bind.
- Path: person -> legacy -> facade (flows F-15, F-11, F-08, F-06, F-02)
- Governance: The panel binds to the edge's facade. A lease sets the person's facade password, delivered to their phone encrypted to their passkey-derived key (C-03), and rotated after the first bind. Offline only break-glass, until an offline hand-over exists (R-11).
- Evidence: KeyClerk change log (lease, hand-over, rotation); facade bind log reported by the agent.
- Residual: The credential is typed on a shared panel (copyable, shoulder-surfable) for one bind; the panel's own session after login is not recorded by ReliKey.
